learn.title: Containers: ACI, Container Apps, AKS
objectives: Explain what a container and a container image are, and why containers are portable and lightweight.
Compare containers with virtual machines and with Azure Functions.
Describe Azure Container Instances, Azure Container Apps and Azure Kubernetes Service.
Choose the right container service for a scenario.
Recognise Azure Container Registry as the place to store private container images.
concepts: A lightweight, isolated package of an application plus its libraries and settings. It shares the host operating system kernel, so it starts in seconds.
A read-only template a container is started from. Build once, run anywhere a container runtime exists.
The best-known platform and format for building and running containers.
The fastest, simplest way to run a container in Azure. No VMs or orchestrator to manage, billed per second. Good for simple apps, task automation and short-lived jobs.
A serverless container platform for microservices and apps. It scales automatically on HTTP traffic or events, including to zero. It's built on Kubernetes, but Kubernetes is hidden from you.
Managed Kubernetes for orchestrating many containers at scale. Azure manages the control plane; you manage and pay for the agent nodes.
Automating deployment, scaling, networking, health checks and updates for many containers.
An architecture that splits an app into small, independently deployable services, which often run in containers.
A private registry for storing and managing container images.
comparisons: A VM virtualizes hardware and runs a full OS. A container virtualizes the OS, so it's smaller and faster to start, and many fit on one host.
ACI runs individual containers simply, with no orchestration. AKS orchestrates many containers with full Kubernetes control.
Container Apps is serverless and hides Kubernetes. AKS exposes the Kubernetes API for full control and more management.
Containers package any app with its dependencies. Functions run small event-driven pieces of code without you packaging an environment.
traps: Containers don't include a full guest operating system.
ACI is not an orchestrator. For many coordinated containers, think AKS or Container Apps.
With AKS, the control plane is managed by Azure, but the worker nodes are VMs you pay for.
Container Apps can scale to zero, so idle apps cost little or nothing for compute.
Azure Container Registry stores images. It doesn't run containers.
revision: One container, quickly, no management: ACI.
Microservices, serverless, scale on events: Azure Container Apps.
Full Kubernetes control at scale: AKS.
Store private images: Azure Container Registry.
Containers = portable, lightweight, fast start, shared kernel.
Containers are an application hosting option alongside web apps and VMs.
